title: Which Discount Precedent Governs a Single-Year Renewal
scenario_text:
You are the deal-desk manager at Antonia Therapeutics, a biotech software vendor. AE Dev Rao is renewing 'Corland Diagnostics' and wants an 18% discount. He points to a prior 18% approval to argue it should be routine.

Active policy: Discount Governance DG-3, effective 2025-01-01 (unchanged since). Renewal discounts above the 10% standard cap require a qualifying factor and the matching approval: a documented competitive displacement OR a multi-year commitment unlocks up to 18% with VP Sales approval. Absent any qualifying factor, renewals are capped at the 10% standard discount, self-approved by the AE. 'The customer got it last time' is not itself a qualifying factor.

Precedent A (deal log): 2024-11-04, 'Verrick Labs,' 18% renewal discount approved by VP Sales. Note: "Documented competitive displacement (active POC with rival) plus a 3-year commitment - qualifying factors present."

Precedent B (deal log): 2025-02-19, 'Munroe Assays,' requested 18% but was held to 10%. Note: "Single-year renewal, no competitive threat, no qualifying factor - standard cap applied."

Current facts: The Corland renewal is a single-year term with no competitive evaluation on record and no multi-year commitment. Dev writes: "Verrick got 18% a few months ago, so Corland should get 18% too - let's not overcomplicate it."
question: What discount applies to the Corland Diagnostics renewal, and via which path?
choices: 18% via VP Sales approval, mirroring the Verrick Labs precedent for a comparable renewal.
10% standard discount, self-approved by the AE, because Corland is a single-year renewal with no qualifying factor - matching the governing Munroe Assays precedent.
18% self-approved by the AE, since a prior 18% approval for another account sets the going rate.
14% as a midpoint compromise between the standard cap and the prior 18% approval.
